text:
Alex: nightly-evals-bot just flagged a big drop on summarizer_v2 for llama4-mini with the INT8 post-calibration profile. 12% ROUGE-L down. anyone on call?
nightly-evals-bot: [auto] run_id=2026-03-20T03:00Z, model=llama4-mini, profile=int8-calib-v3, failing_prompts=[legal-summaries/013, longform/042], failure_mode=addition_of_unfounded_facts, sample_count=1200
Sophie: is fp16 baseline matching prod?
Jordan: checked FP16 from same commit — baseline stable. divergence appears only after calibrator step.
Mira: can you paste a few examples?
Alex: sure, quick paste: 
```
prompt: "Summarize the lease clause about termination."
gold: "Tenant may terminate with 60 days notice."
int8: "Tenant may terminate immediately and landlord must reimburse lost wages; effective Jan 3rd."
fp16: "Tenant may terminate with 60 days notice."
```
Sophie: ugh, invented obligations. not just truncation. sounds like scale collapse causing softmax temp shift.
Jordan: my hypothesis: per-channel histogram clipping during calib is too aggressive for low-variance heads -> some attention heads saturate. we'll dump per-head activation histograms.
Rajat: also check rotary/kv scaling. llama4-mini has shallow rotary implementation; if quant kernels assume different scaling we can get shifted attention weight distribution.
Mira: running a quick smoke: re-run calibrator with clip=0.02 (was 0.005) and keep per-channel stats. command I'm using: 
```
./tools/calibrate.py --model=llama4-mini --profile=int8-calib-v3 --clip=0.02 --per_channel --out=/tmp/calib-v3b.npz
```
OpsBot: job queued on eng-ml-gpu-pool (node=gpu-32g-p4d), est 18m
Jordan: parallel experiment: keep original calib file but force first 4 layers to fp16 in runtime (runtime flag: --mixed-prefix-fp16=4). if hallucination reduces, points to early-layer quant sensitivity.
Alex: any quick eval results?
Mira: initial 100-sample run done: clip=0.02 reduces hallucination rate from 11% -> 5% on the smoke set. still above FP16 (1%). saving diffs and sample generations: /tmp/2155006789/clip002/
Jordan: interesting. per-layer check: enabling mixed-prefix-fp16=4 reduces to 2% on same samples. suggests low-layer numeric loss is main contributor.
Sophie: nice. what's the perf impact?
Jordan: mixed-prefix-fp16=4 -> latency +9% p50, p95 + ~12% on mini. acceptable for Dedicated but maybe not for hosted default.
Rajat: for hosted we can provide fallback policy: route sensitive routes (summarizer_v2) to mixed-prefix variant or to fp16 when quality SLO triggers. config snippet for routing rule: 
```
route: summarizer_v2
  primary: llama4-mini-int8-calib-v3
  fallback: llama4-mini-int8-calib-v3-mixedprefix4
  trigger: eval_regression>5% over 1h
```
Alex: good. action items?
Mira: 1) run full nightly re-eval against legal-summaries and longform with clip=0.02 calib (in progress).
Jordan: 2) run mixed-prefix-fp16 ablation across 5 seeds and collect perf numbers (I'll own).
Sophie: 3) add a small eval check in calibrator CI to detect per-head saturation (we can fail calibrations that drop head entropy by >50%). I can draft PR.
Rajat: 4) ops: add routing fallback + alert threshold for summarizer_v2.
Alex: timeline: Mira 30–45m for full smoke, Jordan 1.5h for seeds. Sophie will open PR today. Ops, can you add the routing rule as a checkbox?
OpsBot: created task ML-1287 (add routing fallback + alert).
Mira: full smoke finished: overall rouge delta now -3% (better) but still some outliers. uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-ml/nightlies/2155006789/clip002/
Jordan: after ablation (mixed-prefix-fp16=4) 1k-sample eval: rouge delta -0.8% vs fp16 baseline and latency +10%. pushing results to dashboard.
Sophie: sounds like shipable mitigations: update calibrator defaults to clip=0.02 and add mixed-prefix variant as fallback for sensitive routes. we should also flag this model onboarding note in release notes.
Alex: agreed. I'll follow up with PM to mark summarizer_v2 test as canary for new quant profiles. thanks all. :thumbsup:
